sentiment.rationale: The document shows genuine operational momentum: Commercial Airplanes operating margin improved from (33.3)% to (20.1)% year-over-year, 737 deliveries increased, and the company resumed 787 deliveries. However, no formal guidance was raised; management's forward language is hedged ('we view 2021 as a key inflection point... while the global pandemic continues to challenge the overall market environment'). The structural risk of the 737 MAX electrical issue and ongoing COVID-19 headwinds prevent a higher score. The score reflects a real trajectory change (inflection point language) without a formal guidance raise.

summary.revenue: $15.2 billion, down 10% year-over-year (from $16.9 billion), primarily driven by lower 787 deliveries and commercial services volume, partially offset by higher 737 deliveries and higher KC-46A Tanker revenue.
summary.eps: GAAP loss per share of ($0.92) and core (non-GAAP) loss per share of ($1.53), reflecting year-over-year KC-46A Tanker improvement, higher 737 deliveries, and lower commercial airplanes period costs, partially offset by lower tax benefits and higher interest expense.
summary.guidance: The 737 program expects to gradually increase production to 31 per month in early 2022 with further gradual increases to correspond with market demand. The 777X first delivery is expected in late 2023. The 787 program transitioned to a production rate of 5 aircraft per month. The combined 777/777X production rate is transitioning to 2 aircraft per month. No formal revenue or earnings guidance was provided.
summary.margin: GAAP operating margin was (0.5)% (improved from (8.0)% in Q1 2020). Core (non-GAAP) operating margin was (2.3)% (improved from (10.1)% in Q1 2020). Commercial Airplanes operating margin improved to (20.1)% from (33.3)%. Defense, Space & Security operating margin increased to 5.6% from (3.2)%. Global Services operating margin decreased to 11.8% from 15.3%.
key_risks: COVID-19 pandemic continues to challenge the overall market environment.
737 MAX electrical issues identified in certain locations in the flight deck of select 737 MAX airplanes, requiring work with FAA and customers to address.
Pre-tax charge of $318 million on the VC-25B program largely due to COVID-19 impacts and performance issues at a key supplier.
Lower 787 deliveries and lower commercial services volume due to COVID-19.
Global pandemic continues to challenge the overall market environment.
key_opportunities: Continued progress on safe return to service of 737 MAX worldwide; 21 airlines have returned fleets to service, safely flying more than 26,000 revenue flights.
Commercial Airplanes secured orders for 100 737 aircraft from Southwest Airlines, 25 from United Airlines, 23 from Alaska Airlines, and four 747 freighter aircraft from Atlas Air.
Defense, Space & Security awarded Lots 6 and 7 contracts for 27 KC-46A Tanker aircraft, a contract for 11 P-8A Poseidon aircraft, and contracts for six V-22 Osprey rotorcraft.
